precepts.text: But I thought the scripture says in a multitude of counsel there's safety. That seems to be the total opposite of what the Bible tells us.
precepts.point: So it says, and let the counsel of your own heart stand. There's no man more faithful unto thee. But I thought the scripture says in a multitude of counsel there's safety. That seems to be the total opposite of what the Bible tells us. Should we not seek counsel? Only a few people know that. Okay, wait a second. Do you all understand that in a multitude of counsel there's safety? What does that mean? In a multitude of counsel there's safety. Who can help me out understand that? Okay. Right there. Keep on, right to the back. Right there. Stand up.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
Sirach says, “And let the counsel of thine own heart stand: for there is no man more faithful unto thee than it.” But the scripture also says, “Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.” At first that seems to be the total opposite. Should we not seek counsel?

In the multitude of counsellors there is safety means that as much counsel as you can get will help you make the right decisions and move in the right direction. That is correct. And the counsel of your own heart can stand only when it is funnelled through the laws of God, through the scriptures. Then you can make your decision and stand on it, because it is based on the laws of God.

Go up to verse 12 and it opens: “But be continually with a godly man, whom thou knowest to keep the commandments of the Lord.” Your everyday life should be spent around godly people, and if you lack understanding, around people with more understanding than you, so you can level up. You know who keeps the commandments by being exercised to discern between good and evil, and every beast consorts with its own kind. Such a man “will sorrow with thee, if thou shalt miscarry”: he will correct you.

So letting the counsel of your own heart stand is not for the man who seeks no counsel and makes his decisions while watching porn. He is going to make a mistake. It is for the man whose mind is godly, like the godly man he took counsel from. “For a man’s mind is sometime wont to tell him more than seven watchmen, that sit above in an high tower.”

“And above all this pray to the most High, that he will direct thy way in truth.” Above your own heart and above the counsel of a friend, you go to God, and God does not hear the prayer of sinners. “Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” So the two scriptures agree: get counsel from the brothers, balance it with what you think is right with a godly mind, then ask God to direct your path.

precepts.text: Answer D is a scary mindset to have. What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound? That is the mindset of the Christian church: I found grace, grace covers me, I can do what I want as long as I believe; I do not have to do what Christ says. That is a terrible mindset, and it is exactly what this verse is warning against.
precepts.point: Correct answer read: the real battlefield is private. A lot of people fall spiritually in secret long before they fall publicly. The representative shows up at the Sabbath; the real you shows up when you are at home, when you are alone, when you are with your family. Your wife knows exactly who you are. You cannot come up here saluting hard like you are over righteous and then go home and verbally, financially, or physically abuse your wife: you lack integrity and you have poor character. And vice versa, sisters: you cannot bow all the way down at the door and then go home and curse your husband out and keep nothing. You lack integrity in that area too.

note.label: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

precepts.why:
The question put to the class: you're alone online late at night, temptation hits, and nobody from the congregation would know. What shows integrity? A, entertain the temptation privately. B, watch a little and justify it later. C, cut it off immediately and fight temptation. D, convince yourself grace covers everything. Answer D is a scary mindset to have, and Paul already answered it: “What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?”

Shall we continue in sin that grace may cover everything? That is a terrible mindset, and it is the mindset of Christianity: I found grace, grace covers me, I can do what I want when I want. All I have to do is believe in Jesus; I ain't got to do nothing he says, just believe he's my Lord and savior. Christianity is evil.

The answer is C. The questions are easy and the answers are easy; the problem is when it comes to fruition in real time. You are fighting your war against yourself: you don't want to push play, but you want to push play, and nobody is there to tell you a damn thing. That is when C gets blurred out.

The real battlefield is private. A lot of people fall spiritually in secret long before they fall publicly. The representative shows up at the Sabbath; the real you shows up at home, alone, with your family, and your wife knows exactly who you are. You can't salute so hard you're over righteous and then go home and verbally, financially or physically abuse your wife. And sisters, you can't bow 90 degrees at the door and then go home, cuss your husband out, and keep a filthy house. That is lacking integrity and poor character.

That is Proverbs 11:3: “The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.” Grace is not a cover for sin; integrity is acting on what you know, even when nobody is watching.

precepts.text: Where no counsel is the people fall, but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.
precepts.point: No brothers counsel the women: senior sisters deal with the sisters and bring matters to leadership when they need judgment; that is the protocol.

note.label: Why Do Fools Fall In Love

precepts.why:
“Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls.” Watching for your souls is a job. Leadership is not about sitting in the front and getting the plates first. There are things you never see, never hear about and never have to deal with, because there are things put in place: the men who deal with the men, whose phones are the first ones to get called, and the senior sisters who deal with the sisters.

“Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.” If you don’t follow counsel, you will fall. A congregation without counsel will fall; there is no way around it.

You have all the wisdom and understanding in front of you. If something is said to you on the phone, you can say hold on, I’ll call you right back, and reach out to a senior brother or senior sister: does this sound right? And they will tell you: no, that doesn’t sound right; no, you can’t do that; no, that’s not wise. You can alleviate a lot of situations that way. But for some reason everybody is grown: oh, I can deal with it. No, you are not in your right mind, obviously. Because of lust you ignore all the red flags, and every red flag you see before you get married is heightened a thousand times after, because you are with them every single day.

The protocol is part of that safety. No brothers should be dealing with the women on any counseling basis. The senior sisters are set up to deal with the women, and if it is a congregational issue, or somebody has to be judged, the senior sisters bring it to leadership and it is dealt with there. That multitude of counsellors is how leadership watches for your soul.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
The wicked join hand in hand by covenant, and Isaiah names that covenant: “Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves.” That is the black pastors and politicians.

“Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation.” This is Christ. “he that believeth shall not make haste”: you will not be confounded; you will not leave this truth.

“Judgment also will I lay to the line, and righteousness to the plummet: and the hail shall sweep away the refuge of lies.” The Lord is bringing judgment. The hail, the destruction, shall sweep away the refuge of Christianity and all its lies, and Islam as well. “And your covenant with death shall be disannulled, and your agreement with hell shall not stand.” All the blacks that made a covenant with the white man, with these fake Israelis, shall have it disannulled; the agreement with hell is this low condition our people are in. “when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, then ye shall be trodden down by it”: those black pastors shall be trodden down.

“From the time that it goeth forth it shall take you”: from the time the teaching goes forth. “for morning by morning shall it pass over, by day and by night: and it shall be a vexation only to understand the report.” Morning by morning, day and night, you are going to hear the proper teaching, and it vexes you, because you already made that agreement for the financial gain.

“For the bed is shorter than that a man can stretch himself on it: and the covering narrower than that he can wrap himself in it.” Whether you are in Christianity or politics, you are trying to get comfortable after hearing the vexing report. You know it is true, but you made that agreement. The bed is your lies and there is not enough room; you try to wrap yourself in your Christian lies, but you already heard the report. That is why the wicked, hand in hand, shall not be unpunished.

The seed of the righteous is built on the tried stone, and “he that believeth shall not make haste”: he will not be confounded and will not leave this truth. precepts.point: Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: much strife and contention comes from messy people. Repent of that messy spirit; it has no place in Israel.

precepts.text: Where no counsel is, the people fall, but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety; Rehoboam rejects the safe counsel of the elders.
precepts.point: The young men advise him to answer roughly, saying his little finger will be thicker than his father's loins, that he will add to their yoke, and chastise them with scorpions instead of whips.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

precepts.why:
“Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.”

Rehoboam rejects the safe counsel of the elders: “he forsook the counsel which the old men gave him, and took counsel with the young men that were brought up with him, that stood before him.” He asks them, “What advice give ye that we may return answer to this people”, including them as if they were rulers with him over the nation.

This is the same error seen constantly among the people: one comes to the truth and seeks counsel from a new brother or sister rather than from the elder men and women already established in the congregation. And the young men's counsel was rough: “My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s loins”, “I will put more to your yoke: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.”

precepts.text: The integrity of the upright shall guide them, but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them; walking upright is integrity even when nobody is watching.
precepts.point: Job says his righteousness he holds fast and will not let it go, and his heart shall not reproach him so long as he lives, saying he is not a hypocrite; what he says, he does.

note.label: Job 27: I Will Not Remove My Integrity From Me

precepts.why:
“The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.” Job says, “My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go: my heart shall not reproach me so long as I live.” He is not a hypocrite; what he says, he does.

Walking upright is integrity even when nobody is watching, and that integrity guides a man. The perverse transgressor, who only gets in order when the righteous come around, is destroyed by his own perverseness. Job holds his integrity till he dies, and it guides him through everything he is going through.

precepts.text: Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not go unpunished, but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.
precepts.point: The only way the wickedness of the wicked comes to an end is that they die. The wicked is the so-called white man according to the bible, and his end is inevitable. This is God's word, not man's; do not try to get God's enemy out of the way.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.” The wicked may join together, hand in hand, but they will not go unpunished. That is the answer to David's prayer that the wickedness of the wicked come to an end.

And the other half of his prayer, “but establish the just”, is answered too: the seed of the righteous shall be delivered. The righteous God tries the hearts and reins, so he knows who is just and who is wicked, and each gets his end.

precepts.text: Riches profit not in the day of wrath, but righteousness delivereth from death.
precepts.point: Riches are uncertain; money in an online bank cannot be reached when Wi-Fi and electricity go out, and then the rich man is in the same boat as the poor.

note.label: Psalm 49: The Vanity of Riches Against the Grave

precepts.why:
“Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.” None of them “can by any means redeem his brother, nor give to God a ransom for him”. Celebrities and rich people watch their family members die and can do nothing about it. All the money for transplants, surgery and chemotherapy cannot save them from the grave if the Most High wants to take them.

What delivers from death is not riches but righteousness. That is why David has no cause to fear in the days of evil: the redemption of the soul is precious, and money does not buy it.

precepts.text: A tale-bearer reveals secrets, but a faithful spirit conceals the matter.
precepts.point: If you reveal the secret, the one who hears it will put you to shame and your bad reputation will not turn away, because now your business is put out there.

note.label: Proverbs 25: The Proverbs of Solomon Copied by Hezekiah's Men

precepts.why:
“Debate thy cause with thy neighbour himself; and discover not a secret to another: Lest he that heareth it put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.” One who reveals a secret to another is a gossiper, a backbiter, a tale-bearer.

Solomon names him: “A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.” You want to be able to trust that what you share is not repeated by others; that is the faithful spirit that conceals the matter, and the talebearer is the opposite.

If you reveal the secret, the one who hears it will put you to shame and your bad reputation will not turn away, because now your business is put out there. Take the cause to your neighbor himself and keep the matter concealed.

That is a lot of us. You get up mad in the car, mad at every driver, everything leaking out all day, and guess who gets it when you get home? Your wife gets the trauma dump. But the narcissist in the video also said there is something he can do: he can plug the holes up. You can fix it. You get counsel, you talk about the issues.
